British Council: Third and mixed conditionals

title: Identify something or add a comment
goal: Choose the right relative clause, pronoun and punctuation.
explanation: A relative clause adds information about a noun. Sometimes that information is needed to identify which person or thing you mean. This defining clause stays attached without commas. Sometimes the noun is already identified and the clause adds a comment; this non-defining clause is separated with commas. The difference can change the message, not just the punctuation. Choose who for people and which for things; that can replace them in many defining clauses, but not in non-defining ones. You can omit an object relative pronoun in a defining clause, but not a subject relative pronoun. Find the subject inside the clause before deciding whether omission is possible.
explanationEs: La relativa especificativa identifica y va sin comas; la explicativa añade información sobre algo ya identificado y se separa con comas. That no se usa en explicativas. Solo puedes omitir el relativo objeto en una especificativa.

uses.title: Identify which one you mean
uses.when: Use a defining relative clause when the detail selects a person, thing or group.
uses.form: Noun + who/which/that + clause, without separating commas.
uses.why: The relative clause limits the reference. Removing it can make the intended group unclear or broader.
uses.es: La información selecciona de qué persona o grupo hablas; no se separa con comas.

examples.en: The residents who work at night need daytime appointments.
examples.es: Los vecinos que trabajan de noche necesitan citas diurnas.
examples.note: The clause selects residents who work at night, not all residents.

examples.en: The form that you need is on the reception desk.
examples.es: El formulario que necesita está en recepción.
examples.note: The clause identifies the particular form.

uses.title: Add information about an identified noun
uses.when: Use a non-defining clause when the reader already knows which person or thing you mean.
uses.form: Identified noun, who/which + clause, remaining sentence.
uses.why: Commas mark the added comment. Do not use that or omit the relative pronoun in this structure.
uses.es: Usa who/which y comas para información adicional; no that ni omisión.

examples.en: Our only meeting room, which seats twelve people, is upstairs.
examples.es: Nuestra única sala de reuniones, con capacidad para doce personas, está arriba.
examples.note: Only meeting room is already identified; the seating detail is additional.

examples.en: Ms Green, who coordinates the volunteers, will contact you.
examples.es: La señora Green, que coordina al voluntariado, se pondrá en contacto con usted.
examples.note: The name identifies the person; the clause adds her role.

uses.title: Check whether the relative pronoun is subject or object
uses.when: Omit the pronoun only when it is the object of a defining clause.
uses.form: Object: the course (that) I chose. Subject: the course that starts tomorrow.
uses.why: Look for a separate subject after the pronoun. I chose has a subject; starts tomorrow needs that as its subject.
uses.es: Identifica quién realiza el verbo de la relativa antes de omitir nada.

examples.en: The course I chose includes individual feedback.
examples.es: El curso que elegí incluye comentarios individuales.
examples.note: I is the subject of chose; the omitted relative pronoun would be its object.

examples.en: The course that starts tomorrow includes individual feedback.
examples.es: El curso que empieza mañana incluye comentarios individuales.
examples.note: That is the subject of starts, so it cannot be omitted.

glossary.definition: A clause that adds information about a noun, often beginning with who, which or that.
glossary.es: Cláusula relativa: añade información sobre un sustantivo.

glossary.definition: Information needed to identify the intended person, thing or group.
glossary.es: Detalle especificativo: información necesaria para identificar la referencia.

takeaway: Decide whether the detail identifies or comments, then check the pronoun's job.

writingBridge.prompt: Write four sentences recommending a course. Identify a group of learners, add a comment about a named tutor, describe a course you selected and identify one that starts soon.
checklist: Defining details have no separating commas.
Additional comments use commas and who/which, not that.
Any omitted relative pronoun is an object, not the clause's subject.

sources.title: British Council: Relative pronouns and clauses

title: Explain reasons, contrasts and results
goal: Choose a connector for the logical relationship and build a complete sentence.
explanation: A connector tells the reader how ideas relate. Decide the relationship before choosing the word: is the second idea a reason, an unexpected contrast or a result? Then check the structure that follows. Because and although introduce clauses with a subject and verb. Because of and despite introduce a noun phrase or an -ing form. A longer connector does not automatically improve an argument. Therefore marks a result, but it does not join two complete sentences with a comma alone. Use a full stop or semicolon in that pattern. Finally, check the logic: grammatically correct sentences can still use because or therefore to suggest a connection the information does not support.
explanationEs: Primero decide la relación entre ideas. Because/although llevan oración; because of/despite, nombre o -ing. Therefore necesita puntuación adecuada. Un conector correcto no convierte automáticamente una asociación en causa.

uses.title: Explain a reason
uses.when: Use because before a clause and because of before a noun phrase.
uses.form: Because + subject + verb; because of + noun phrase or verb-ing.
uses.why: The meaning is similar, but the grammar after each expression is different. An opening because-clause needs a main clause.
uses.es: Because lleva sujeto y verbo; because of lleva un grupo nominal. No dejes una subordinada aislada.

examples.en: The workshop was postponed because the tutor was ill.
examples.es: El taller se aplazó porque el tutor estaba enfermo.
examples.note: Because introduces the complete reason clause the tutor was ill.

examples.en: The workshop was postponed because of the tutor's illness.
examples.es: El taller se aplazó debido a la enfermedad del tutor.
examples.note: Because of introduces the noun phrase the tutor's illness.

uses.title: Express an unexpected contrast
uses.when: Use although before a clause and despite before a noun phrase or an -ing form.
uses.form: Although + subject + verb; despite + noun/verb-ing; despite the fact that + clause.
uses.why: The main outcome is unexpected in light of the other information. Do not add but to the main clause after although.
uses.es: Although y despite contrastan con estructuras diferentes. Evita duplicar although…but.

examples.en: Although the room was small, everyone had a seat.
examples.es: Aunque la sala era pequeña, todos tenían asiento.
examples.note: The clause presents a contrast between limited size and enough seating.

examples.en: Despite arriving early, we had to wait outside.
examples.es: A pesar de llegar temprano, tuvimos que esperar fuera.
examples.note: Despite takes arriving; we is the understood subject of both actions.

uses.title: Show a supported result
uses.when: Use so to coordinate a cause and result, or therefore with sentence boundaries that support it.
uses.form: Complete clause, so + complete clause; complete sentence. Therefore, complete sentence; or use a semicolon before therefore.
uses.why: Therefore is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction. Also check whether the claimed result follows from the stated reason.
uses.es: So puede enlazar dos oraciones; therefore necesita punto o punto y coma antes en este patrón.

examples.en: The only entrance was blocked, so we could not enter.
examples.es: La única entrada estaba bloqueada, así que no pudimos entrar.
examples.note: The blocked only entrance directly explains the inability to enter.

examples.en: No tutor is available on Friday. Therefore, we need to choose another day.
examples.es: No hay ningún tutor disponible el viernes. Por tanto, debemos elegir otro día.
examples.note: The full stop separates complete sentences; therefore signals the result.

glossary.definition: A group of words built around a verb, usually with a subject.
glossary.es: Cláusula: grupo estructurado alrededor de un verbo, normalmente con sujeto.

glossary.definition: A noun with any words that belong with it, such as the tutor's illness.
glossary.es: Sintagma nominal: un sustantivo con sus acompañantes.

takeaway: Check the relationship, the following structure and the sentence boundary.

writingBridge.prompt: Write a short paragraph of four sentences about changing a timetable. Explain a reason, acknowledge a difficulty and draw a practical conclusion.
checklist: Each connector matches the actual relationship between ideas.
Because/although and because of/despite have the correct following structure.
The conclusion is supported and therefore does not create a comma splice.

title: Ask politely and report messages
goal: Keep statement order inside indirect questions and adapt reported messages to their context.
explanation: Indirect language lets you ask for information politely or report a message without quoting every word. These are related structures but different tasks. A present polite request does not automatically need a past tense: could you tell me where the room is asks about its current location. Inside the information clause, use statement order. For a reported message, consider who is speaking now, when the original message was spoken and whether it is still true. Past reporting often brings a tense shift, but it is not always necessary for information that remains true. Change pronouns and time expressions only when the new context requires it. Keep the original meaning, certainty and responsibility intact.
explanationEs: Una petición indirecta actual no exige pasado: Could you tell me where the room is? Al contar un mensaje, adapta tiempos, pronombres y referencias según el contexto. No cambies todos los tiempos mecánicamente ni aumentes la certeza del original.

uses.title: Make a polite information request
uses.when: Put a direct question inside a polite opening while keeping statement order in the inner clause.
uses.form: Could you tell me + wh-word + subject + verb? Do you know + if/whether + subject + verb?
uses.why: The outer clause carries the question structure. The embedded clause does not repeat do-support or subject-verb inversion.
uses.es: La pregunta principal usa inversión; la parte interna mantiene sujeto + verbo.

examples.en: Could you tell me where the office is?
examples.es: ¿Podría decirme dónde está la oficina?
examples.note: The office comes before is inside the request.

examples.en: Do you know whether the fee includes materials?
examples.es: ¿Sabe si la tarifa incluye los materiales?
examples.note: Whether introduces the original yes/no question; use includes, not does include.

uses.title: Report statements without changing their meaning
uses.when: Use a reporting verb and adapt time and pronouns to the reporting situation.
uses.form: Said (that) + clause; told + person + (that) + clause. Past reporting may shift the tense back.
uses.why: Tell normally needs a person in this reporting pattern; say does not take the person directly. Present tense can remain when the information is still true.
uses.es: Distingue said that y told me that. Cambia tiempos solo según la perspectiva temporal y la vigencia.

examples.en: The organiser told me that the workshop had been cancelled.
examples.es: El organizador me dijo que el taller se había cancelado.
examples.note: Told names the listener; had been cancelled places cancellation before the report.

examples.en: The receptionist said that the office opens at nine; that is still its regular opening time.
examples.es: La recepcionista dijo que la oficina abre a las nueve; ese sigue siendo su horario habitual.
examples.note: Opens remains present because the reported timetable still applies.

uses.title: Report questions and requests
uses.when: Use statement order for a reported question and an object + to-infinitive for a reported request.
uses.form: Asked + person + if/wh-clause; asked/told + person + to + base verb; negative: not to + base verb.
uses.why: A report of a question is normally a statement, so it does not need a final question mark. A request reports an action someone should take.
uses.es: Las preguntas relatadas conservan orden afirmativo. Las peticiones usan asked someone to do o not to do.

examples.en: She asked me when I could attend.
examples.es: Me preguntó cuándo podía asistir.
examples.note: When I could attend uses statement order; the whole sentence reports a question.

examples.en: The tutor asked us not to share the access link.
examples.es: El tutor nos pidió que no compartiéramos el enlace de acceso.
examples.note: Not comes before to share in this negative request.

glossary.definition: A question used inside a larger clause, with statement word order.
glossary.es: Pregunta integrada: pregunta dentro de otra estructura, con orden afirmativo.

glossary.definition: A move to an earlier verb tense when reporting from a later viewpoint.
glossary.es: Cambio retrospectivo: desplazamiento verbal al contar desde otro momento.

takeaway: Keep inner question clauses in statement order and adapt reported messages by context.

writingBridge.prompt: Write four sentences to a course coordinator: make a polite location question, ask whether materials are included, report one statement and report one request.
checklist: Indirect questions use subject + verb in the inner clause.
Say/tell/ask patterns include any required person.
Reported tense, pronouns and certainty preserve the original meaning.

title: Make sentence boundaries clear
goal: Build complete sentences and use punctuation to show their structure.
explanation: Punctuation helps the reader see where one complete thought ends and another begins. First find the subject and the main verb, then check whether the sentence can stand on its own. A clause beginning with because or although normally depends on another clause; leaving it alone can create a fragment in formal writing. Two complete sentences need more than a comma between them. Use a full stop, a suitable conjunction or a semicolon when the relationship is close. Apostrophes have different jobs: they can mark missing letters or possession, but they do not normally make a noun plural. Edit structure before adding commas, because commas cannot repair a missing main clause.
explanationEs: Primero delimita las oraciones completas. Una subordinada aislada puede ser un fragmento; dos oraciones completas no se unen solo con coma. El apóstrofo marca posesión o contracción, no un plural normal.

uses.title: Complete a dependent thought
uses.when: Attach a dependent clause to a main clause in formal connected writing.
uses.form: Because/although + clause, main clause; or main clause + dependent clause.
uses.why: A dependent clause may contain a subject and verb but still leave the reader waiting for the main message.
uses.es: Tener sujeto y verbo no siempre basta: una subordinada necesita completar su relación con otra oración.

examples.en: Because the room was unavailable, we moved the meeting online.
examples.es: Como la sala no estaba disponible, trasladamos la reunión a internet.
examples.note: The main clause completes the reason introduced by because.

examples.en: Although the course was useful, I needed more practice.
examples.es: Aunque el curso fue útil, necesitaba más práctica.
examples.note: The second clause supplies the contrasting main point.

uses.title: Separate complete sentences
uses.when: Use a full stop, a coordinating conjunction or a semicolon between independent clauses.
uses.form: Sentence. Sentence. / clause, but/so/and + clause / clause; clause.
uses.why: A comma alone is too weak to join two independent clauses in this formal writing pattern. A semicolon suits closely connected statements.
uses.es: Evita unir dos oraciones completas solo con coma. Elige punto, conjunción o punto y coma según la relación.

examples.en: The form was complete, but the signature was missing.
examples.es: El formulario estaba completo, pero faltaba la firma.
examples.note: But connects the two complete clauses and expresses contrast.

examples.en: The reception desk was closed; the online service was still available.
examples.es: La recepción estaba cerrada; el servicio en línea seguía disponible.
examples.note: A semicolon links closely related complete clauses without a conjunction.

uses.title: Use apostrophes and capitals accurately
uses.when: Use apostrophes for contractions and noun possession, and capitals for sentence starts and proper names.
uses.form: It's = it is/it has; singular noun + 's; regular plural ending in s + '; ordinary plurals without apostrophes.
uses.why: Possessive its is an exception without an apostrophe. A capital letter signals a sentence start or a specific name, not general importance.
uses.es: Its no lleva apóstrofo. Distingue plural, posesión singular y posesión plural.

examples.en: The students' room is next to the tutor's office.
examples.es: La sala de los estudiantes está junto al despacho del tutor.
examples.note: Students' is plural possession; tutor's is singular possession.

examples.en: The centre changed its hours. It's now open on Monday evenings.
examples.es: El centro cambió su horario. Ahora abre los lunes por la tarde.
examples.note: Its shows possession; it's means it is. Monday is capitalised.

glossary.definition: A clause that can stand as a complete sentence.
glossary.es: Cláusula independiente: puede funcionar como oración completa.

glossary.definition: Two independent clauses joined by only a comma.
glossary.es: Unión incorrecta por coma: dos oraciones completas enlazadas solo con coma.

takeaway: Find complete clauses first; punctuation should make their relationship visible.

writingBridge.prompt: Write a four-sentence update about a rescheduled workshop. Include an opening because-clause, a contrast, two related independent clauses and a possessive noun.
checklist: No dependent clause is left as an unintended fragment.
No two independent clauses are joined only by a comma.
Apostrophes and capital letters have a clear grammatical purpose.

title: Add variety without losing precision
goal: Use a range of structures to express accurate relationships, clear references and measured claims.
explanation: Grammatical range means being able to choose different structures when the meaning needs them. It does not mean making every sentence long. A clear paragraph may combine a short claim, a longer explanation and a precise example. Check reference so that this, it and they have an obvious meaning. Keep items in lists parallel so the reader can compare them easily. Use language such as may, tends to and in some cases when the claim has limits, and explain those limits. More advanced structures, including participle clauses, are useful only when their subjects and meanings remain clear. The goal is controlled choice: each structure should help the reader follow the idea.
explanationEs: La variedad consiste en elegir estructuras útiles, no en alargar todas las frases. Mantén referencias claras, listas paralelas y afirmaciones proporcionadas. Las estructuras avanzadas solo ayudan si conservan significado y control.

uses.title: Vary structure to explain a relationship
uses.when: Use a simple sentence for a direct point and a complex sentence when a reason, condition or contrast needs expressing.
uses.form: Clear main clause; main clause + a relevant subordinate clause.
uses.why: A subordinate clause earns its place by adding a useful relationship. Remove length that only repeats the same idea.
uses.es: Una subordinada debe aportar una relación concreta. Alterna estructuras según lo que necesites comunicar.

examples.en: The centre needs more evening appointments.
examples.es: El centro necesita más citas por la tarde.
examples.note: A simple sentence states the proposal directly.

examples.en: More evening appointments would help residents who cannot leave work during the day.
examples.es: Más citas por la tarde ayudarían a los vecinos que no pueden dejar el trabajo durante el día.
examples.note: The relative clause identifies the group and explains the proposal's relevance.

uses.title: Keep references and lists clear
uses.when: Use a named reference when a pronoun is ambiguous, and keep coordinated items in matching forms.
uses.form: This + specific noun; parallel verb phrases or noun phrases in a list.
uses.why: Clear reference reduces guessing. Parallel structure lets the reader compare actions at the same grammatical level.
uses.es: Aclara this con un nombre y mantén la misma forma en los elementos de una lista.

examples.en: The service needs to reduce delays, improve access and publish clearer instructions.
examples.es: El servicio necesita reducir retrasos, mejorar el acceso y publicar instrucciones más claras.
examples.note: The three actions share the same base-verb structure after needs to.

examples.en: The booking system lost several requests. This failure caused avoidable delays.
examples.es: El sistema de reservas perdió varias solicitudes. Este fallo causó retrasos evitables.
examples.note: This failure identifies exactly what the second sentence refers to.

uses.title: Limit claims and control advanced clauses
uses.when: Use qualified language when evidence supports a tendency, and participle clauses only with a clear shared subject.
uses.form: May + base verb; tend to + base verb; participle phrase, main clause with the same understood subject.
uses.why: A qualification should match a real limit. An opening participle phrase normally describes the main clause's subject, not a different person.
uses.es: Matiza cuando haya límites reales. En una cláusula de participio, comprueba que el sujeto implícito coincida con el de la principal.

examples.en: Flexible hours may improve access for people with irregular work schedules.
examples.es: Un horario flexible puede mejorar el acceso para quienes tienen horarios laborales irregulares.
examples.note: May avoids promising a universal effect, and the group is specified.

examples.en: Having checked the timetable, the coordinator confirmed the appointment.
examples.es: Tras comprobar el horario, la coordinadora confirmó la cita.
examples.note: The coordinator both checked and confirmed; the earlier completed action uses having checked.

glossary.definition: Matching grammatical forms for items serving the same role in a list or comparison.
glossary.es: Paralelismo: usar formas equivalentes en elementos de la misma lista o comparación.

glossary.definition: Language that limits the strength or scope of a claim.
glossary.es: Matización: limitar la fuerza o el alcance de una afirmación.

takeaway: Use variety to make the meaning clearer, then check reference, parallelism and claim strength.

writingBridge.prompt: Write a short paragraph of four or five sentences proposing a more accessible public service. Include a direct proposal, an explanation, a qualified benefit and a list of matching actions.
checklist: Sentence structures serve distinct purposes instead of repeating the same point.
Pronouns or this + noun have clear references; listed actions are parallel.
The benefit is appropriately limited and any participle clause has a clear shared subject.
